senses.gloss: A painful viral illness that raises a burning rash in a band across the skin.
examples: My aunt came down with *shingles* right after the move.
The vaccine cuts your risk of *shingles* after fifty.
*Shingles* left a rash across his ribs for three weeks.

senses.gloss: A large group of fish swimming together.
examples: A *shoal* of silver fish turned all at once under the boat.
Dolphins drive *shoals* of herring into a tight ball.
The diver swam straight through a *shoal* of tiny blue fish.

senses.gloss: A curved piece of iron nailed to the bottom of a horse's hoof.
examples: The mare threw a *shoe* on the trail and came up lame.
The farrier nailed a new *shoe* onto each front hoof.
Worn *shoes* make a horse slip on hard ground.

senses.gloss: A session of taking photographs or filming.
examples: The magazine *shoot* took all morning on the roof.
She booked a family photo *shoot* for the fall.
Both *shoots* were rained out and had to be rescheduled.

senses.gloss: A video game whose action is built around firing weapons.
examples: He plays first-person *shooters* with his cousins online.
The studio's new *shooter* sold two million copies.
I'm terrible at *shooters* but I love racing games.

senses.gloss: A school class in which students learn woodworking or metalworking.
examples: He built a birdhouse in *shop* last semester.
*Shop* was the only class he looked forward to.
The high school cut both *shop* and home economics.

senses.gloss: The front passenger seat of a car, next to the driver.
examples: My brother called *shotgun* before we reached the driveway.
You rode *shotgun* the whole way here.
Whoever gets to the car first gets *shotgun*.

senses.gloss: A performance given in front of an audience, such as a play or a concert.
examples: The *show* starts at eight, so let's eat early.
We caught a late *show* at a club downtown.
Both *shows* sold out in a single afternoon.

senses.gloss: A public event where things are put on display or judged.
examples: We spent Saturday at the auto *show*.
Her collie won best in breed at the dog *show*.
Galleries all over town open new *shows* on the first Friday.

senses.gloss: Something that covers and hides what is underneath.
examples: The valley disappeared under a *shroud* of morning fog.
The whole deal was kept behind a *shroud* of secrecy.
Smoke lay over the city in a gray *shroud*.

senses.gloss: One of the people or groups opposing each other in a fight, an argument, or a game.
examples: Whose *side* are you on?
Neither *side* would agree to a compromise.
The losing *side* shook hands and walked off the field.

senses.gloss: A small dish of food served along with the main course.
examples: The sandwich comes with a *side* of fries.
I ordered coleslaw as my *side*.
Their *sides* are better than their main dishes.

senses.gloss: One branch of a family, traced through the mother or the father.
examples: The red hair comes from my mother's *side*.
Everyone on his father's *side* is tall.
The two *sides* of the family met for the first time at the wedding.

senses.gloss: A short private conversation at the judge's bench, out of the jury's hearing.
examples: The judge called both attorneys up for a *sidebar*.
After a brief *sidebar*, the question was withdrawn.
The transcript leaves out whatever was said in the *sidebars*.

senses.gloss: A short track beside a railroad's main line where cars can be parked or passed.
examples: The freight train pulled onto a *siding* to let us by.
Old boxcars sat rusting on a weedy *siding*.
The mill had its own *siding* for loading lumber.

senses.gloss: The device on a gun or telescope that you look through to aim.
examples: He adjusted the rear *sight* before the first shot.
The buck stepped right into his *sights*.
Cheap *sights* drift after a few hundred rounds.

senses.gloss: One of the twelve parts of the zodiac that a person is born under.
examples: What's your *sign*?
She reads the horoscope for every *sign* but her own.
The two of them were born under the same *sign*.

senses.gloss: A written mark standing for a word, a number, or an operation.
examples: Put a dollar *sign* in front of the number.
The kids are learning the plus and minus *signs*.
He wrote the equals *sign* twice by mistake.

senses.gloss: Forks, knives, and spoons, especially the good set kept for guests.
examples: Grandma got out the good *silver* for Thanksgiving.
He polished the *silver* the night before the party.
The *silver* is in the bottom drawer of the hutch.

senses.gloss: The medal given for second place.
examples: She took *silver* in the two hundred meters.
The team settled for *silver* after losing the final.
Nobody remembers who won *silver*.

senses.gloss: A creature of myth whose beautiful singing lured sailors onto the rocks.
examples: The sailors plugged their ears against the *sirens*.
Easy money is a *siren* that has wrecked plenty of careers.
The novel's *siren* draws every man in the village to ruin.

senses.gloss: A woman who belongs to a religious order.
examples: A *sister* in a gray habit answered the door.
The *sisters* run a school on the other side of town.
She spent thirty years as a teaching *sister*.

senses.gloss: A place on the internet where a person or company keeps its pages.
examples: Their *site* has been down all morning.
You can order tickets on the theater's *site*.
He blocks news *sites* while he's working.

senses.gloss: A short comic scene in a stage or television show.
examples: The opening *sketch* made fun of the debate.
She wrote *sketches* for a late-night show.
That *sketch* about the airport is a classic.

senses.gloss: The outer layer of a fruit or vegetable.
examples: I bake the potatoes with the *skins* on.
Peel the *skin* off the peach before you slice it.
Grape *skins* give red wine its color.

senses.gloss: A thin film that forms on the surface of a liquid.
examples: A *skin* had formed on the pudding.
Stir the paint so it doesn't develop a *skin*.
He blew the *skin* off his cocoa before drinking it.

senses.gloss: A thick flat piece cut from something such as meat, cheese, or stone.
examples: He cut a *slab* of cheddar off the block.
The butcher wrapped a *slab* of ribs in white paper.
The counter is a single *slab* of marble.

senses.gloss: A long cut made by a sweeping stroke of something sharp.
examples: There was a *slash* across the canvas of the painting.
A thorn left a *slash* on the back of his hand.
Deep *slashes* in the sidewall had flattened all four tires.

senses.gloss: A list of candidates, or a set of events planned one after another.
examples: The party put up a full *slate* of candidates.
The studio announced its *slate* for next year.
We have a light *slate* of games this weekend.

senses.gloss: Someone completely controlled by a habit, a feeling, or a routine.
examples: He's a *slave* to his phone.
I refuse to be a *slave* to fashion.
Dairy farmers are *slaves* to the milking schedule.

senses.gloss: A person thought of in terms of how deeply or lightly they sleep.
examples: I'm a light *sleeper*, so any noise wakes me.
He's such a heavy *sleeper* that he slept through the alarm.
The *sleepers* in the next tent never stirred.

senses.gloss: Something that becomes a success after nobody expected it to.
examples: The movie was a *sleeper* that ran for months.
Their second album turned into a quiet *sleeper*.
Scouts love finding *sleepers* in the late rounds.

senses.gloss: A stiff paper or plastic cover that something slides into.
examples: The record was still in its original *sleeve*.
The barista slipped a cardboard *sleeve* onto my cup.
He keeps the discs in paper *sleeves*.

senses.gloss: A smooth sloping structure that children climb up and slide down.
examples: She went down the *slide* headfirst.
The park put in a new twisting *slide*.
Both *slides* were too hot to touch by noon.

senses.gloss: One page of a presentation shown on a screen.
examples: Go back to the *slide* with the sales figures.
He crammed six charts onto one *slide*.
Her presentation ran to forty *slides*.

senses.gloss: A small glass plate holding a sample to be viewed under a microscope.
examples: Put a drop of pond water on the *slide*.
The lab labels every *slide* with a date.
He clipped the *slide* onto the microscope.

senses.gloss: A small hamburger served on a soft little bun.
examples: We ordered a plate of *sliders* to share.
Each *slider* comes with pickles and grilled onion.
The bar sells *sliders* three for eight dollars.

senses.gloss: A fast baseball pitch that breaks sideways as it reaches the plate.
examples: He struck him out on a nasty *slider*.
Her *slider* breaks late and low.
Young pitchers throw too many *sliders*.

senses.gloss: A light dress-shaped undergarment worn beneath a dress or skirt.
examples: She wore a silk *slip* under the thin dress.
The lining had pulled away from the *slip*.
*Slips* are hard to find in stores now.

senses.gloss: A small careless mistake, especially in speaking.
examples: It was just a *slip* of the tongue.
One *slip* in the code cost them a whole day.
He apologized for the *slip* and moved on.

senses.gloss: In math, a number showing how steeply a line rises or falls.
examples: Find the *slope* of the line through those two points.
A horizontal line has a *slope* of zero.
The two graphs have the same *slope* but different starting points.

senses.gloss: A coin-operated gambling machine.
examples: She spent the whole evening at the *slots*.
The casino floor is wall-to-wall *slots*.
He won forty dollars on a quarter *slot*.

senses.gloss: Laziness and unwillingness to work.
examples: He blamed the delay on plain *sloth*.
*Sloth* is one of the seven deadly sins.
A summer of *sloth* left the yard a jungle.

senses.gloss: A lump of lead fired from a gun.
examples: The surgeon dug a *slug* out of his shoulder.
A single *slug* went through the door.
Deer season here is *slugs* only, no buckshot.

senses.gloss: A large mouthful of a drink, especially liquor.
examples: He took a *slug* of coffee and kept driving.
She poured a *slug* of bourbon into the batter.
Two *slugs* of that stuff and he was done for the night.

senses.gloss: A false story spread in order to damage someone's reputation.
examples: The ad was a *smear*, and everyone knew it.
He called the accusation a political *smear*.
*Smears* like that follow a candidate for years.

senses.gloss: The sense that lets you notice odors through your nose.
examples: Dogs rely on *smell* far more than on sight.
She lost her sense of *smell* after the infection.
*Smell* brings back memories faster than any other sense.

senses.gloss: A covered cooker that cooks meat slowly in hot smoke.
examples: He runs the *smoker* all night before a party.
Brisket needs twelve hours in the *smoker*.
Backyard *smokers* start at a couple hundred dollars.

senses.gloss: An unexpected problem that holds something up.
examples: We hit a *snag* with the permits.
The move went off without a *snag*.
A few small *snags* pushed the opening back a week.

senses.gloss: A long flexible metal coil pushed down a drain to clear a clog.
examples: The plumber ran a *snake* down the kitchen drain.
You can rent a *snake* at the hardware store.
Neither the plunger nor the *snake* opened the pipe.

senses.gloss: A person who betrays others while pretending to be a friend.
examples: He turned out to be a *snake*.
Don't trust her with that; she's a *snake*.
*Snakes* like that will smile at you and take your job.

senses.gloss: A short sharp sound made by something breaking or shutting.
examples: We heard the *snap* of a twig behind us.
The lid closed with a satisfying *snap*.
Small *snaps* came from the fire all evening.

senses.gloss: A short spell of unusually cold weather.
examples: A late cold *snap* killed the tomato plants.
The *snap* lasted four days and then it warmed up.
Early *snaps* like that are rough on the citrus groves.

senses.gloss: Something very easy to do.
examples: The test was a *snap*.
Changing the filter is a *snap*.
Getting the kids to bed is never a *snap*.

senses.gloss: The sharp-sounding drum at the center of a drum kit.
examples: The song opens with a single hit on the *snare*.
He tightened the *snare* between songs.
Marching bands put the *snares* in the front row.

senses.gloss: A tangled mass of something such as hair, wire, or stopped traffic.
examples: The wind left a *snarl* in her hair.
The accident caused a two-hour traffic *snarl*.
He worked the *snarls* out of the fishing line.

senses.gloss: A fitting that a plug or a light bulb goes into.
examples: There's only one *socket* in the whole bedroom.
The bulb wouldn't screw into the *socket*.
All the *sockets* on that wall are dead.

senses.gloss: A hollow in the body that another part fits into.
examples: He popped his shoulder out of its *socket*.
Her eyes were sunk deep in their *sockets*.
The dentist packed the empty *socket* with gauze.

senses.gloss: A white powder used to make baked goods rise.
examples: The recipe calls for a teaspoon of *soda*.
Baking *soda* takes the smell out of the fridge.
We were out of *soda*, so the biscuits came out flat.

senses.gloss: The land of a particular country, thought of as its territory.
examples: It was the first attack on American *soil* in years.
He hasn't set foot on his native *soil* since he was twelve.
Foreign troops were never allowed on their *soil*.

senses.gloss: The series of musical sounds that a bird or a whale makes.
examples: The wood thrush has the loveliest *song* in the forest.
Researchers recorded the whales' *songs* all winter.
You can tell most warblers apart by *song* alone.

senses.gloss: The spring or lake where a river begins.
examples: They hiked all day to the *source* of the river.
The creek's *source* is a spring under the ridge.
Both rivers have their *sources* high in the mountains.

senses.gloss: A thing that provides or produces something.
examples: Beans are a cheap *source* of protein.
Tourism is the town's main *source* of income.
They traced the smell back to its *source*.

senses.gloss: A playing card of the suit marked with black pointed leaf shapes.
examples: He led with the ace of *spades*.
*Spades* were trump for that hand.
She had four *spades* and nothing else worth playing.
